sentences.text: On 23.07.1976, a notification under Section 3(1) of the Karnataka Acquisition of Land for Grant of House Sites Act, 1972 (for short, "the Act") was published.

entities.text: Karnataka Acquisition of Land for Grant of House Sites Act, 1972

sentences.text: After considering the cause shown, the State Government decided to over-rule the objections and proceeded to issue a declaration as contemplated under Section 3(4) of the Act, on 05.07.1982.

2. Petitioners approached this Court by filing W.P.Nos.37331-333/1982, W.P.Nos.38122-123/1982,
W.P.Nos.4039 and 40180/1982 challenging the notification NC: 2024:KHC:9881 issued under Section 3(1) of the Act and also the declaration issued under Section 3(4) of the Act.
This Court, by order dated 04.09.1987, dismissed the writ petitions and thereby upheld the notification and also the declaration.
3. This order of the learned Single Judge has attained finality.
4. Subsequently, an award was passed on 03.10.1989 and this was once again the subject matter of challenge by the petitioners in W.P.No.6852/1990 and WP.Nos.10144- 151/1989.
This Court, by order dated 04.06.1998, negated the contentions of the petitioners that awards were illegal.

5. This Court while upholding the award also directed that the respondents should take steps to form sites and distribute the same to the persons belonging to weaker sections of the society and also passed an order that the respondents should not sell the sites in public auction as it would amount to defeating the very purpose of acquisition NC: 2024:KHC:9881 of lands.
This order upholding the awards has also attained finality, inasmuch as the matter was not carried further.

Thus, in respect of a preliminary notification of the year 1976, the award that had been passed was also upheld by an order of this Court on 04.06.1998.
6.

Fourteen years thereafter, the petitioners once again approached this Court in W.P.Nos.21177-21193/2012 seeking for a declaration that the lands of the petitioners from amongst 33 acres 7 guntas notified had lapsed and the acquisition had been rendered void.

This Court by Sri. Thimme Gowda vs The Principal Secretary on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32655797/
5 order dated 11.12.2013 came to the conclusion as follows:
"3.

sentences.text: While the matter was argued at length, it was observed by this court that the petitioners claim to be possessed of large families, who have lost their primary source of livelihood in their lands having been acquired.
They are, in fact, living without proper shelter and a livelihood and in order to accommodate them, it was suggested that the respondents provide sites to each of the petitioners.

The respondents pointed out that the entire land that has been acquired as per the layout plan would be just sufficient to be distrivuted amongst the NC: 2024:KHC:9881 beneficiaries, who have been already identified, apart from taking into account other common areas and amenities to be provided, which would be required for the beneficial enjoyment of the house sites that are formed.

But after obtaining further instructions, it was reluctantly stated that the petitioners can be accommodated in providing a 30' x 40'
site, each.

4. The learned Counsel for the petitioners however, were not satisfied with the offer and were inclined to seek sites of larger dimensions in order to give up their claim and give a quietus to the proceedings.

In the interest of justice however, since the petitioners have lost their valuable lands and it is not also on record that they have received compensation in respect of the lands so acquired, either by volition or default, it is not unjust in the petitioners being conferred such a benefit by the respondents providing each of them a site measuring 30' x 40'.
5.

This court is also conscious of the fact that it is possible that other land owners,
who are similarly placed as the petitioners, would cite this as a precedent in also seeking such benefit.
It is made clear that as the circumstances stand, there is no possibility of providing any further sites for any other land owners, who may not have approached this court till date.

As the challenge to the acquisition NC:
2024:KHC:9881 proceedings has lasted several decades by a series of petitions being filed and it is in order to ensure that there is no further impediment for the speedy implementation of the project, that this measure of directing the respondents to provide a site each to the petitioners is warranted.
With the above observations, the petition stands disposed of."

7. Thus, the challenge to the acquisition on the ground that it had lapsed was also not accepted by this Court, but the Court ordered that in order to ensure that there is no further impediment for the speedy implementation of the Project, each of the petitioners should be given a site measuring 30' x 40'.
8.
The petitioners, being aggrieved, preferred a Writ Appeal in W.A. No.279-295 of 2014.

However,
the Division Bench of this Court concluded that the appeal had been filed only to persuade the respondents to allot sites larger than 30' X 40', and there was no merit in the appeal, and it proceeded to accordingly dismiss the appeal.

Thus, the challenge to the acquisition on the Sri. Thimme Gowda vs The Principal Secretary on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32655797/
6 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:9881 ground that it had lapsed was also negated by this Court and affirmed by the Division Bench also.

In my view, having regard to the fact that the challenge to the acquisition on the ground that it had lapsed, was negated by the learned Single Judge of this Court and also confirmed by the Division Bench, it would be impermissible for the petitioners to file the present writ petition seeking for a declaration that the acquisition had lapsed because of sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 24 and Section 25 of the 2013 Act.

sentences.text: It is to be noticed here that the petitioners had, in fact, challenged the award on the ground that it was beyond the period of two years prescribed under Section 11A of the 1894 Act, and this challenge of theirs was negated by this Court.

This, by itself, indicates that an award had been passed and the challenge to the legality of the award on the ground that it was beyond the stipulated time was untenable.
12.

In light of the award having been upheld in the earlier round of litigation, the present writ petition challenging the acquisition on the ground that the award had not been passed and possession had not been taken cannot be sustained.
The Writ Petition is, therefore, dismissed.

13. At this stage, the learned counsel for the petitioners sought to contend that the lands had remained unutilized and therefore, there was no justification for continuing the acquisition proceedings.
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:9881 14.

It is to be stated here that the lands could not be put to use only because of the litigation that had been initiated by the petitioners, and the petitioners cannot be permitted to put forth this ground to seek quashing of the acquisition nearly 50 years after the notification had been issued.
This argument is, therefore, rejected.

16. The learned counsel for respondent No.4 also states that sites have already been earmarked for allotment and he would be filing the layout plan in which the sites to be allotted to the petitioners would also be earmarked clearly.
17. Respondent No.4 shall accordingly convey the sites demarcated in the layout plan to the petitioners in compliance of the order passed by this Court earlier.
Subject to the above, the writ petition is dismissed.

rpc_texts: The Writ Petition is, therefore, dismissed.

Respondent No.4 in its statement of objections has acknowledged the fact that the petitioners had accepted the offer of site measuring 30' x 40' and they, therefore, accept the fact that the sites measuring 30' x 40' would have be allotted to each of the petitioners.
17. Respondent No.4 shall accordingly convey the sites demarcated in the layout plan to the petitioners in compliance of the order passed by this Court earlier.
Subject to the above, the writ petition is dismissed.
